title: One package plugs into all three tiers: the Reactor runs its reducers, Connect renders its editors, Switchboard runs its processors
content:
When you build on Powerhouse you ship one artefact: a package bundling document models (schemas plus reducers), editor components, and processors. You do not ship a browser build and a server build. The same package plugs into the whole stack, and each tier picks up the part that belongs to it.

## The division of labour

- The **Reactor** picks up your reducers and runs them whenever an action is dispatched.
- **Connect** renders your editor components so users can interact with documents.
- **Switchboard** runs your processors, which fold the operation stream into read models and expose them over GraphQL.

Three consumers, one bundle. As the Academy puts it: you write the logic once, and the stack decides where it executes.

## Why it matters

This is what makes "install a package" a meaningful unit of capability rather than a partial delivery. A package is not a library you then have to wire into three places — it is a complete vertical slice. Adding it to a deployment adds the document type, its UI, and its derived data at once, and nothing about the package changes depending on where it lands.

## The mental model

Read the package as declarative and the tiers as interpreters. The package says *what* exists: this is the schema, these are the legal transitions, this is how it looks, this is what should be derived from it. Each tier reads the portion addressed to it and ignores the rest. Connect never looks at your processors; Switchboard never mounts your React components.

## What follows from it

The routing is by module kind, not by configuration, so there is no manifest step where you tell each host which parts to take — and no opportunity for the three tiers to disagree about which version of the logic they are running. It also sets the boundary for where code belongs: UI concerns in the editor module, state transitions in the reducer, derived reads in the processor. Put something in the wrong module and it simply never executes, because no tier is looking for it there.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/02-architecture/01-the-big-picture.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
